channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

item.title: [DW] Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

item.title: [DW] Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding.
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

item.title: [DW] Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

item.title: [DW] UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
item.description: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

item.title: [DW] Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
item.description: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?

item.title: [DW] UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
item.description: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.

item.title: [DW] Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
item.description: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe led on abortion – now the neo-conservative backlash is stalling the final push
item.description: The general trend of abortion care has been on the up, but the effect of neo-conservatism's modern revamp has been impossible to ignore. From Rome to Budapest, governments have been rolling back the progress, with initiatives stalling all the way up to EU level.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Le Pen and Mélenchon are ‘economically illiterate’ and weaponising migration, says French scholar ahead of 2027 race
item.description: French political scientist Jacques Rupnik says the economic illiteracy of Marine Le Pen and Mélenchon is astonishing. He anticipates that in the first round of France's presidential election, most voters will back a candidate they believe can stop Le Pen. A Mamdani moment could happen, since people feel that politics has exhausted itself.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How does Trump’s AI pact compare with the EU?
item.description: Donald Trump is betting on voluntary commitments from AI companies. On Tuesday (29 September), he unveiled a self-regulatory agreement drawn up with some of the biggest names in the AI industry.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU accession of Moldova and Ukraine is alternative to Nato, as Russia draws new Iron Curtain in Europe
item.description: With Nato doors closed to Ukraine and Russia pushing a new Iron Curtain across the Black Sea, an “urgent” EU expansion toward Kyiv and Chișinău is emerging as Europe’s main tool to defend its eastern flank and preserve its global clout.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s children will inherit public-health crisis from new EU pesticide approvals
item.description: By extending pesticide approvals and keeping hazardous products on the market, Brussels is bending to Big Pharma and causing a food-system and public-health burden for decades to come.

item.title: [DW] Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

item.title: [DW] Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
item.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmakers has resigned.

item.title: [DW] EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
item.description: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

item.title: [Financial Times] Low-profile hedge fund smashes record for New York office rent
item.description: Castle Hook will pay up to $21.2mn a year for 53,000 sq ft of penthouse space at developer Related’s new Madison Avenue tower

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Maxi merde’: French presidential campaign rattled by a week of chaos
item.description: Nobody has emerged unscathed, but the spotlight is firmly on the far left and the far right.

item.title: [EU Observer] G7 releases diesel stocks after Trump pressure, EU denies caving
item.description: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of emergency oil and fuel stocks after weeks in which Washington pressed European capitals to open their diesel reserves. Brussels said US threats played no part.

item.title: [Financial Times] US economy adds just 29,000 jobs in September as hiring slows sharply
item.description: Figure renews market debate about outlook for further Fed rate rises

item.title: [Politico Europe] Polanski’s Greens look for their next opening
item.description: The left-wing populist party nudged Keir Starmer out of office, but now Andy Burnham is drawing satisfied protest voters back to Labour.

item.title: [Financial Times] EU pushes Ukraine for further reforms to unlock funding
item.description: Brussels rebuffs request for additional support this year as Kyiv’s parliament struggles to pass promised changes

item.title: [EU Observer] The war changes yet again: Ukrainians use domestic missile for first time as Russians launch assault on bridges (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,681)
item.description: A defence analyst warned that Russia is mass-producing "thousands" of new drones “far more dangerous and faster" than jet-powered Shaheds which Ukraine cannot yet stop.

item.title: [Financial Times] US backs down from fuel export ban threat as G7 agrees to release 100mn barrels
item.description: G7 leaders said after a meeting on Friday that they would release 100mn barrels of crude and diesel

item.title: [Financial Times] Eurozone inflation hits three-year high of 3.8%
item.description: Consumer prices rose at higher rate than expected in September

item.title: [Financial Times] Why does Anthropic’s IPO feel so weird?
item.description: Compared to other blockbuster share sales, the build-up to the AI company’s stock market debut has felt discordant, even creepy

item.title: [EU Observer] Brunner takes victory lap on irregular arrivals as Syrian asylum claims collapse for reasons beyond EU policy
item.description: Syria's regime collapsed in December 2024, over 22 months ago. The country was the largest source of irregular arrivals in 2023. Today, the EU disingenuously attributes its migration policies for the drop of arrivals.

item.title: [Financial Times] Quant hedge funds reap big gains from global bond sell-off
item.description: Trend-following portfolios have latched on to sharp rise in yields this year as Iran war and strong US economic data fuel inflation fears

item.title: [EU Observer] French far-right leader Bardella denies writing antisemitic messages
item.description: Jordan Bardella, a leader of the French far-right National Rally, has denied writing antisemitic messages in 2013.

item.title: [Politico Europe] 17 countries join forces to oppose EU budget cuts
item.description: Italy and Romania lead push to preserve EU spending for agriculture and regional payouts.

item.title: [Financial Times] Israel’s top court overturns ban of Arab parties in upcoming election
item.description: Supreme Court’s unanimous ruling clears way for Ra’am and Joint List to run and potentially swing balance in event of hung parliament

item.title: [Politico Europe] G7 agrees to release oil reserves after U.S. push
item.description: France said the agreement meant the U.S. would not ban the export of diesel.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Šefčovič: Verhandlung mit China noch ohne Ergebnisse
item.description: Der EU-Handelskommissar erklärt gegenüber POLITICO, China habe verstanden, dass eine Einigung dringend notwendig ist. Er hofft auf Ergebnisse zu drei Hauptthemen.

item.title: [EU Observer] Magyar waives his own immunity, as Hungary targets billions in alleged fraud and two former Orbán ministers in custody (Day 143 of the Tisza government)
item.description: PM Peter Magyar waives his own immunity as Hungary's "Operation Purgatory" saw authorities detain two former Orbán ministers over alleged multibillion-forint corruption. The new asset recovery office took over four major cases, including Orbán's brother's visa business, while Hungary may soon join the European Public Prosecutor's Office.

item.title: [EU Observer] From the Netherlands to Sierra Leone: EU aid, a president’s daughter and Europe’s most‑wanted cocaine boss
item.description: Jos Leijdekkers was sentenced in the Netherlands in absentia to 24 years in prison for smuggling seven tonnes of cocaine, robbery, and ordering a killing. But he is also the partner of Agnes Bio, the president of Sierra Leone's daughter.

item.title: [Financial Times] My mortgage is a problem for the Fed, and for America
item.description: Homeowners like me are staying put, the market is frozen and affordability is as ugly as it was in the housing bubble

item.title: [Politico Europe] G7 to hold emergency talks over possible diesel release
item.description: The meeting comes as Trump threatens to ban U.S. diesel exports.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Frankreich erwägt Freigabe von Öl- und Dieselreserven nach US-Druck
item.description: Paris hat vorgeschlagen, 100 Millionen Barrel Rohöl und Diesel freizugeben. Eine offizielle Bestätigung gibt es noch nicht. Deutschland will den Forderungen Washingtons noch nicht nachgeben.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Feijóo: In Ceuta, it’s up to Europe to clean up the Spanish government’s mess
item.description: Europe must reckon with the failure of the leadership in Madrid and do everything to prevent a worsening of the crisis.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ceuta has become a laboratory for the degradation and dehumanisation of migrants
item.description: We went to Ceuta to see how Europe treats people who arrive at its borders. We came back asking how Europe can still call itself a continent governed by law. What we saw there was the often abstract failure of migration policy made brutally concrete: the daily humiliation of human beings.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tories warn Burnham’s EU ‘pandering’ will shred post-Brexit trade deals
item.description: Three former ministers tell POLITICO of “grave consequences” if the U.K. moves closer to the EU under prime minister's bid for a revamped relationship.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Diesel : sous la pression des Etats-Unis, l’exécutif envisage de libérer une part importante de ses réserves
item.description: L’exécutif français a proposé aux autres pays européens de mettre sur le marché 100 millions de barils de pétrole brut et de gazole. Une concession majeure envers les Etats-Unis.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why young men are drawn to the far right and young women to the far left
item.description: Gender now splits the youngest voters more than class or education. Many young men feel sidelined by a shifting balance and vote far-right while young women vote far-left.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s Affordable Housing Act must look beyond short-term rentals
item.description: As Brussels pins its housing fix on curbing Airbnb-style rentals, campaigners warn lawmakers are ducking a far bigger fight over Europe’s millions of empty homes and the people still sleeping rough.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Are EU countries allowed to bring back border controls whenever they want?
item.description: Italy brought back border controls with Spain in August, and has now extended them until at least 15 October, as more EU countries introduce checks.

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin has told military leaders to abandon rules of war, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Ukrainian leader tells FT his Russian counterpart has given the order that ‘there are no rules now’

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump’s short-sighted diesel gamble
item.description: Yes, Nixon’s export ban did briefly suppress domestic prices but it had a huge long-term cost

item.title: [Financial Times] US refiners reap windfall profits as wars push up fuel prices for consumers
item.description: Oil producer income has drawn scrutiny but lower-profile refiners have posted a fourfold increase in margins

item.title: [Financial Times] AI got smarter. The bills got harder to control
item.description: Powerful AI tools are burning through budgets, prompting a rethink of how the technology is priced ahead of frontier lab IPOs
